doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Working with Kai: billing and audiences
summary: The names flip-flopped; they shared the writing and audiences enjoyed the sight of two sliding trombones.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: How did you decide [whether] it would be Jay & Kai or Kai & Jay?
We never did. It would flip-flop. It would flip-flop from engagement to engagement.
That group was together for a comparative good period of time. Two years – something like that?
A little better than two years, uh huh.
Were there any particular performing experiences or recording experiences across that time that you would like to share with us?

Hmm. None that stand out. We both enjoyed the format. It was fun to look forward to going to work every night. It was fun to record and to write. We were both writers. Kai was a good arranger. We shared the writing chores and what not. It was always a nice experience to look forward to performing with Kai and recording with him. And the audiences responded to the sight of two guys up there on the stand, slides going crazy. It was a visual experience. People found it to be a visual thing that they enjoyed.
